judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the image in hero carousel slide 2 of 9. It is the only content of a link to /eletronicos (sorted by price), and the link takes its name from it. Its alt is the placeholder "Descriptive text for the image". The crop shows a Black Friday banner for small appliances ("Todos os eletroportáteis em até 10x sem juros ou 10% off à vista no PIX", "Compre agora"). The alternative names neither the destination nor the offer, so the link's purpose is lost and 1.1.1 fails for a control (H30/G82). The claim says exactly this. Live page: the server-rendered data still holds this slide with the same image and CTA and no alt value, so the capture matches.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the newsletter field #newsletter-email (type=email, required), labelled by "ex.: nome@email.com", in the form "Não fique de fora das novidades! Preencha com seu email...". It asks for the user's own email address, which is an input purpose listed for 1.3.5. Neither the input nor the form has an autocomplete attribute, so the purpose is not exposed through the HTML autocomplete mechanism (H98). type=email only constrains the format; it does not say that the address is the user's own. The live page renders on the client, so I could not see its markup, but the newsletter section config is unchanged and offers no autocomplete option. Nothing suggests a difference from the capture.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer link "Black Friday" to /black-friday, the Black Friday 2026 landing page, in the "Institucional" column; "Institucional" is a styled paragraph, not a heading. The claim holds for the capture. Two links in the accessibility tree are named Black Friday: this one, and the header nav "BLACK FRIDAY" to /colecao-completa. The category image link is named "Black Friday BLACK FRIDAY" and also goes to /black-friday, and a hidden mobile copy is out of the tree. The two links do not share a context by this rubric's list. The footer link is preceded by the h3 "Não fique de fora das novidades!", while no heading precedes the header link. Their list items hold only the link, and neither has a title. So R1 does not put them in one set. On its own, the text "Black Friday" describes its destination, the Black Friday landing page, so the link meets 2.4.4. If both were judged together, the header link would be the one whose name fits its destination (the full product listing) less well. The live navbar and footer data are unchanged.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header search input (in a role=search form), named by aria-label "O que você procura?". So something on screen does tell users to enter a search term: the visible prompt plus the adjacent search button (G167). 3.3.2 is met and the claim is false. The live navbar config is unchanged.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the only control besides Close in a modal popup with aria-label "Live Sawary Jeans". It is an image link to /colecao-completa, the full product listing. aria-label="Confira" ("check it out") sets its name, and the banner image inside has alt="". The image shows a different offer: 10% OFF EXTRA on the first purchase over R$79,99 with coupon BEMVINDO10, "APROVEITE". "Confira" says nothing of the destination. The link has no title or description, no sentence or list item, and no heading before it; a dialog's name is not in the rubric's context list. Even if "Live Sawary Jeans" counted, it names another campaign. 2.4.4 fails, and the claim names this. The popup is not ambiguous to users in general, since sighted users see the offer. Live data still has the PopupBanner (imageOnly, same image, alt "", title "Live Sawary Jeans", CTA "Confira" to /colecao-completa), shown once per session. The empty alt on a text image is also a 1.1.1 issue.
